content.title: Mary Elizabeth Winstead Calls Life in Scotland with Ewan McGregor and Son 'Heaven for Me' (Exclusive)
content.text: NEED TO KNOW Mary Elizabeth Winstead tells PEOPLE about her life now with husband Ewan McGregor and their 4-year-old sonThe family splits their time between Los Angeles and Scotland, the Hand That Rocks the Cradle actress shares“Just being at our house” and “picking apples," she says, is “heaven for me” Mary Elizabeth Winstead is in heaven with Ewan McGregor and their son Laurie. The American actress, 40, has been “more and more” in her husband’s native Scotland, she shares with PEOPLE. “We have been spending our time between L.A. and Scotland,” says Winstead, 40. “We're kind of settling in a little bit.” At their house near Perthshire, the family spends plenty of time outdoors, says Winstead, who stars in the new remake of The Hand That Rocks the Cradle (now streaming on Hulu). “As much as I love working and as grateful as I am,” the actress says, an ideal weekend is just like a recent one in Scotland. “[It] was very wholesome, very simple, and I was like, ‘If I could just choose what heaven is going to be, this is heaven for me,’” she says. “Just being at our house and cooking. We have an apple tree, and picking apples and being outside and being in nature — having nothing else to do — it's just perfect.” (Left-right:) Clara McGregor, Jamyan McGregor, Laurie McGregor, Anouk McGregor, Ewan McGregor and Mary Elizabeth Winstead at Ewan McGregor's Hollywood Walk of Fame Star in 2024. Frazer Harrison/Getty Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE's free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer​​, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories. Winstead and McGregor, 54, tied the knot in 2022 after costarring on season three of FX drama Fargo. They’ve since worked together in 2024’s A Gentleman in Moscow and hope to find another “funny and heartfelt” project, she says, “because that's how we are at home.” Related Stories Being a mother to Laurie, 4, “is taking up the most space, and that's how I like it,” says Winstead of life these days, which involves babysitting help from Laurie's four half-sisters from McGregor's previous marriage. “Then I always have to carve out time for my artistic self and my working self and all those things. So I guess trying to figure out what that's going to look like in this next era is exciting.” Turning 40 last November has given the Scott Pilgrim alum an opportunity to do so this year. “It does feel like the start of a new era, which is kind of unknown to me, but I think it's all great things. I'm really, really excited for my forties. I'm excited for this feeling of openness, I guess, to whatever's going to come, and I don't really feel like I'm forcing anything… Yeah, I'm liking that feeling.” Mary Elizabeth Winstead and Ewan McGregor on April 29. Alan Chapman/Dave Benett/Getty Next up in Winstead and McGregor’s idyllic life is her Halloween in Scotland, she adds. “I think there'll be some pumpkin picking and carving, and trick-or-treating, the usual. I'm sure we'll be slapping it together somewhat last minute, that tends to be our style.” The Michelle Garza Cervera-directed, Micah Bloomberg-adapted Hand That Rocks the Cradle, costarring Maika Monroe, Raúl Castillo and Martin Starr, is now streaming on Hulu. Among McGregor’s upcoming screen projects is Flowervale Street, in theaters Aug. 14, 2026.
